title: WHAT IF YOU WOKE UP 100 YEARS IN THE FUTURE?

segments.line: The ocean didn't flood the city.
So the first thing you learn about the future: the map changed.
The United Nations ran the numbers.
In 2018, for the first time in all of history, people over 65 outnumbered children under five.
Fewer babies, longer lives, a world that got older instead of bigger.
The machine that proves it is called ITER.
It doesn't make electricity itself — that's the next reactor's job.
The first proof came in December 2022.
The experts say real fusion power plants show up in the 2040s or 2050s.
Humans landed on Mars in the late 2030s.
A Mars trip takes two and a half to three years.
You spent your whole life thinking Mars was a poster on a classroom wall.
Time travel has a catch nobody mentions.

shots.note:
Jake in a white room, ceiling panels glowing soft blue. Camera: slow push-in. Detective
sneaks in the background, behind the door frame, in shadow.
Phone screen close-up: the date reads November 14, 2126. POV shift to Jake's hand holding it.

Detective faces camera, magnifying glass in hand. Timer appears top corner: 23:59:59.
Camera: hold still. OPEN LOOP: the choice is the hook — the viewer must stay to see it.
The 24-hour rule lands by ~10s.

Wide shot: Jake steps out onto a street. The road is there. Water glints at the end of it.
Camera: slow pull back.

shots.line: The ocean didn't flood the city.
shots.note:
The old boardwalk, now a sea wall. People walk on top of it. A kid fishes off the wall.
Camera: gentle pan right.
On-screen text: "+0.28 to +1.01 m by 2100." Detective points at the number. Camera: slow push-in.

A child splashes at the base of the wall. Jake watches, shoes dry by half a step.
Camera: hold still.

shots.line: So the first thing you learn about the future: the map changed.
shots.note: Jake looks back at his street, then at the water. Camera: slow push-in on Jake.

Detective faces camera. The timer ticks in the corner: 22:41:07. Camera: hold still.
RE-HOOK: promise the next chapter's surprise.
A park. Old people playing chess. A few children. Nobody in a rush. Camera: gentle pan left.

shots.line: The United Nations ran the numbers.
shots.note: On-screen text: "10.3 BILLION — peak, mid-2080s." Detective points. Camera: slow push-in.

The chess players. One of them is 94 and sharp as a tack, beating a teenager.
Camera: hold still.
On-screen text: "72.6 years (2019) → 77.1 (2050) → ~82 (2100)." Camera: slow push-in.

shots.line: In 2018, for the first time in all of history, people over 65 outnumbered children under five.
shots.note:
Jake sits on a bench next to an old woman. She smiles. He smiles back, nervous.
Camera: hold still.

shots.line: Fewer babies, longer lives, a world that got older instead of bigger.
shots.note: Detective faces camera. Timer: 20:12:44. Camera: slow push-in. RE-HOOK: promise a visual payoff.
Night. The city glows, but there are no smokestacks. No power lines humming. Camera: slow pull back.

CUTAWAY: a power station cut open like a cake. Inside, a glowing ring. The outside of the
building stays in frame. Camera: slow dive in toward the ring.

shots.line: The machine that proves it is called ITER.
shots.note: On-screen text: "500 MW out from 50 MW in." The plasma pulses. Camera: hold still.

shots.line: It doesn't make electricity itself — that's the next reactor's job.
shots.note: Jake stares up at the reactor. The Detective stands beside him. Camera: slow push-in.

shots.line: The first proof came in December 2022.
shots.note: On-screen text: "Ignition: December 2022." A lab, a flash of light. Camera: hold still.

shots.line: The experts say real fusion power plants show up in the 2040s or 2050s.
shots.note: Detective faces camera. Timer: 17:58:31. Camera: slow push-in. RE-HOOK: promise the Mars payoff.
Night sky. A red dot moves steadily across the stars. Jake points up. Camera: slow push-in.

shots.line: Humans landed on Mars in the late 2030s.
shots.note:
Mars, red dust, a small habitat dome. Four figures in suits walk between buildings.
Camera: slow pull back.

shots.line: A Mars trip takes two and a half to three years.
shots.note:
On-screen text: "2.5–3 YEARS. 7–9 months each way." A ship coasts between two planets.
Camera: gentle pan.

Inside the habitat. A crew eats dinner together. A window shows red dust outside.
Camera: hold still.

shots.line: You spent your whole life thinking Mars was a poster on a classroom wall.
shots.note: Jake looks up at the sky again. The red dot is gone. Camera: slow push-in on Jake.

Detective faces camera, magnifying glass up. Timer: 14:20:05. Camera: slow push-in.
RE-HOOK: promise the decision chapter + a character.

A food stall. Steam. A woman about Jake's age serves noodles. She looks up and smiles like
she's seen him before. Camera: slow push-in. DIALOGUE BEAT begins — two-shot, Jake and Mara.

DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Only the speaker moves; the listener reacts small (one nod).
Jake speaks first, facing Mara.
DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Mara speaks; Jake goes still and listens, one small nod.
DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Jake speaks; Mara listens, head tilt.
DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Mara speaks; Jake listens.
DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Jake speaks, quieter. Mara listens, still.
DIALOGUE BEAT: two-shot. Mara speaks, looks toward the stall next door. Jake listens.

PHONE TEXT SCENE: notification banner pops at the top — "Lena — tell him the sea took the
old pier, 21:47." Cut to the full phone screen in Mara's hand: grey bubbles left, blue replies
right, bubbles appearing one at a time. Caption at the bottom narrates. Camera: hold still.
Mara looks at Jake. The timer ticks: 02:14:33. Camera: slow push-in.
Detective faces camera. Timer: 01:58:02. Camera: hold still. RE-HOOK: the deadline is the hook.
The white room again. The machine hums. The timer counts down: 00:09:41. Camera: slow push-in.

shots.line: Time travel has a catch nobody mentions.
shots.note: Jake stands in front of the machine. Mara waits by the door. Camera: slow push-in on Jake.
The timer hits 00:00:00. The machine flashes. The room goes white. Camera: hold still, then cut to black.
Jake's bedroom, 2026. Morning light. His phone says November 14, 2026. Camera: slow pull back.

Jake sits up, smiling. The Detective is in the corner, scratching his head under the
question mark. Camera: slow push-in.
